description:
Summary:

`_rename_unbacked_to` raised `AssertionError(f"{orig_s} -> {dest}")` when the
symbol being renamed (`orig_s`) already had a replacement that was itself an
unbacked symbol (`dest`).

This is hit when the same op's unbacked binding is rebound across multiple
retrace passes -- e.g. re-exporting / re-lowering an ExportedProgram whose graph
already carries `unbacked_bindings`, so a data-dependent op such as
`aten._unique2` is registered by both `ExportedProgram.module()` and
`PropagateUnbackedSymInts`. In that situation `orig_s`, `new_s` and `dest` all
denote the same runtime value, so aborting is unnecessary.

Fix: drop the assert and generalize the dest-reconciliation into a single unify
step, factored into the helper `_unify_unbacked_aliases`. `orig_s`, `new_s`,
`dest`, and `new_s`'s transitively-resolved replacement
(`existing = self._find(new_s)`) all denote the same value, so we pick one
terminal -- preferring a backed expr -- and redirect every remaining unbacked
alias onto it via `_set_replacement`. This preserves the transitive unification
(`orig_s -> new_s -> terminal`) while covering the corner cases below.

Corner cases handled by the generalized unify:
- Transitively-backed `existing`: `existing` is resolved with `_find`, not a
  one-hop `replacements[new_s]` lookup, so a chain `new_s -> unbacked -> backed`
  surfaces the backed terminal. A one-hop lookup would see the intermediate
  unbacked symbol, pick an unbacked terminal, and overwrite `unbacked -> backed`
  -- silently losing the backed resolution.
- Backed `existing`: if `new_s` resolves to a backed symbol, routing
  `new_s -> dest` (unbacked) would downgrade a backed resolution to an unbacked
  alias. Preferring a backed terminal pins the unbacked `dest` at the backed
  symbol instead, so backedness is never lost.
- Unbacked `existing`: if `new_s` resolves only to another unbacked symbol, it
  is redirected onto the same terminal too, so nothing is left dangling.
- Deterministic terminal choice (first backed alias, else `dest`) keeps the
  result reproducible for `record_shapeenv_event` replay / translation
  validation.

Does not hide a genuine inconsistency:
- `_set_replacement` refines/intersects value ranges and raises
  `ValueRangeError` when two aliases are provably different (disjoint ranges),
  so a real conflict still surfaces at bind time.
- If `_set_replacement` instead silently declines a substitution (target range
  not a subset), we emit a `signpost_event("dynamic",
  "rename_unbacked_to_unify_skipped", ...)` + log so the unreconciled alias is
  observable rather than silent.
- The residual case (same range, different value) is caught downstream by
  AOTInductor runtime size asserts and the lowering's inference-parity check.

Applied to both the `fbcode` and `xplat` copies of `symbolic_shapes.py`.

Test Plan:
New unit tests in `test/test_dynamic_shapes.py` (all pass):
  buck2 test @//mode/opt fbcode//caffe2/test:dynamic_shapes -- test_rename_unbacked_to
  => Pass 4. Fail 0.
- `test_rename_unbacked_to_unifies_unbacked_dest`: benign duplicate binding now
  unifies (`orig -> new -> dest`) instead of raising.
- `test_rename_unbacked_to_raises_on_disjoint_ranges`: a provably-different
  (disjoint-range) rename still surfaces `ValueRangeError` rather than being
  silently unified.
- `test_rename_unbacked_to_preserves_backed_dest`: when `new` already resolves
  to a backed symbol it is not downgraded -- both `new` and the unbacked `dest`
  end up resolving to the backed symbol.
- `test_rename_unbacked_to_unifies_existing_unbacked`: when `new` already
  resolves to another unbacked symbol, that symbol is unified onto the same
  terminal rather than left dangling.
